title: The Wobbly Tower Trick
markdown:
Gather 'round, adventurers! I remember a sunny day in Whispering Woods when our tummies rumbled for yummy, ruby-red berries. But oh, they were high up! Too high.

"We need a tower!" chirped Noah, the little bluebird.
"A cushion tower!" rumbled Buttons, the fluffy bear cub.

Our first try was a bouncy tumble. Noah sat on a cushion, Buttons added another. Wibble-wobble! Down they went in a heap of giggles.

"Let's try again," I said. "Put the biggest, softest cushion at the very bottom!"

Buttons nudged the giant cushion into place. It was a wide, soft base. Then a medium cushion, then a smaller one. Noah hopped on top.

He stood tall and steady! No wobbles!

"Hooray!" Noah chirped.
"It didn't wobble!" Buttons clapped.

"That's the secret of building things that stand up strong!" I explained. "When the heaviest bits are low down, everything is balanced. It keeps everything steady."

Noah and Buttons looked at their tower, then the berries. Perfect! They happily munched.

"So, heavy things on the bottom make it stand up straight?" asked Buttons.
"Exactly!" I beamed. "It's a wonderful way to build!"

"I wonder," Noah chirped, "what other wobbly things could we make steady?"

And so, we learned a fantastic trick: putting the heaviest parts in the best place helps you build amazing things!
characters: Noah the nest helper, Buttons the bear cub, Ranger Tess
